tools.name: list_boat_archetypes
tools.description:
List the 7 boat archetypes with descriptive metadata.

        The LLM (or user) maps a commercial model (e.g. "Sun Odyssey 32") to one
        of these archetypes from the metadata — there is no server-side mapping.

tools.name: get_marine_forecast
tools.description:
Fetch wind (and sea, when available) for a point and time window.

        Args:
            lat: latitude in degrees.
            lon: longitude in degrees.
            start: ISO-8601 datetime, timezone-aware (e.g. "2026-05-01T06:00:00+00:00").
            end: ISO-8601 datetime, timezone-aware.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "plan_passage" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Plan an A→B passage. Compare departure windows by default; pin a single departure only when the user gives an explicit time. ## Tool routing: read this first Be…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Anomalously long tool description
findings.detail: Description of "plan_passage" is 7747 chars, far longer than this server's median (513). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

evidence.snippet: Plan an A→B passage. Compare departure windows by default; pin a single departure only when the user gives an explicit time. ## Tool routing: read this first Be…

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "plan_passage" stacks urgency/override words (always, never, bypass). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

evidence.snippet: Plan an A→B passage. Compare departure windows by default; pin a single departure only when the user gives an explicit time. ## Tool routing: read this first Be…

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: read_me, plan_passage · Public sink: plan_passage · Destructive: plan_passage.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: read_me, plan_passage · Public sink: plan_passage · Destructive: plan_passage

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
